symptoms: leaf: Small water-soaked lesions initially Lesions surrounded by yellow-green halo Lesions expand and coalesce into large necrotic areas Irregular brown necrotic spots as disease progresses Severe cases: extensive defoliation, reduced vigor pod: Dark, sunken lesions with greasy appearance Discolored or shriveled seeds
description: Halo blight is a bacterial disease of beans caused by Pseudomonas syringae pv. phaseolicola. It is seedborne and thrives under cool, humid conditions.
management: cultural_control: Use certified disease-free seeds Crop rotation with non-hosts Avoid overhead irrigation Proper field sanitation chemical_control: Copper-based bactericides to suppress spread Seed treatments to prevent early infection genetic_control: Planting resistant varieties to reduce reliance on chemicals
